# Review pack: Nuh and the flood

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/nuh.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Nuh's story is told in many surahs. The chapters group the repeated passages by theme and reading order; they are NOT a chronology, and surah order is not time order. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Nuh, the flood and his people. None is used in this draft.
- The verses 11:35 and 11:49 are asides addressed to the one receiving the revelation, within the account; they are not used in the story texts, and a reviewer should decide whether to add a note on them.
- The extent of the flood (the whole earth or the region of Nuh's people) is not stated in the verses; the draft says so and does not choose.
- The sense of tannur (11:40, 23:27), of dusur (54:13) and of waqar (71:13) is left open in the texts.
- The Quran gives a span of a thousand years less fifty years (29:14); the verse does not say whether it is his life or his time of calling, and the draft keeps the verse's wording.
- The verse 71:25 (drowned, then made to enter a fire) is reported as written; how it is understood is left to the reviewer.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: names for Nuh's wife, sons and the mountain; the ship's dimensions. None is used in the story texts.
- The chapters group repeated passages by theme. The Quran does not give a chronology across the surahs, so the order of chapters is a reading order only.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Sent to his people  (`#sent-to-his-people`)

Cited ayat: 7:59, 11:25-26, 23:23, 26:105-110, 71:1-4

> **7:59** لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ

### Claims

**c1** (26:106, 7:59, 11:25, 23:23, 71:1): God sent Nuh to his people; one passage calls him their brother.

**c2** (7:59, 23:23): Nuh told them to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him.

**c3** (26:108, 26:110, 71:3): Nuh told them to fear God and to obey him.

**c4** (71:1): God told Nuh to warn his people before a painful punishment came to them.

**c5** (7:59, 11:26): Nuh told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day, and of a painful day.

**c6** (11:25, 71:2, 26:107): Nuh described himself to them as a plain warner and as a trustworthy messenger.

**c7** (26:109): Nuh told them that he asked them for no reward for it, and that his reward was with the Lord of the worlds.

**c8** (71:4): Nuh told them that if they obeyed, God would forgive them some of their sins and give them time until a stated term, and that God's term, when it comes, is not put back.

**c9** (26:105): The Quran says that the people of Nuh denied the messengers.

### One-minute summary

God sent Nuh to his people to call them to worship God alone; he warned them of a coming punishment and asked no reward [c1][c2][c4][c7].

### Complete story

God sent Nuh to his people; one passage calls him their brother [c1]. He told them to worship God, since they had no deity other than Him [c2], to fear God and to obey him [c3]. God told Nuh to warn his people before a painful punishment came to them [c4], and Nuh told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day [c5].

Nuh described himself as a plain warner and a trustworthy messenger [c6]. He told them that he asked them for no reward, because his reward was with the Lord of the worlds [c7]. He also told them that if they obeyed, God would forgive them some of their sins and allow them time until a stated term, and that God's term, once it comes, is not put back [c8]. The Quran says that the people of Nuh denied the messengers [c9].

### Deep study

The same call appears in more than one place (7:59, 11:26, 23:23 and 71:3) with the same core: worship God and fear Him [c2][c3]. The description of the punishment differs by passage: a great day (7:59), a painful day (11:26), a painful punishment (71:1) [c4][c5].

### Kids mode

God sent Nuh to his people [c1]. He told them to worship God alone, to be mindful of God, and to obey him [c2][c3]. He warned them of a punishment to come, and he did not ask them for any reward [c4][c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The Quran presents Nuh as a caller who warns and asks for nothing in return [c4][c7]. One reading is that sincerity in giving advice is shown by not asking for gain from it [c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not say when or where Nuh lived, how many people were in his community, or what their land was called.
- It does not give Nuh's family line or his age when he was sent.
- It does not describe what the people worshipped before Nuh came, beyond the names given in 71:23 (see the chapter on the long call).
- The passage at 26:105 speaks of 'the messengers' in the plural although it concerns Nuh's people; the verse does not explain this wording.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts give Nuh a lineage and names for his family; none is used here.

### Claims

**c1** (7:60): The leaders of Nuh's people said that they saw him in clear error.

**c2** (7:61, 7:62): Nuh replied that he was not in error but was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, delivering his Lord's messages, advising them, and knowing from God what they did not know.

**c3** (7:63): Nuh asked whether they were astonished that a reminder from their Lord had come on a man from among them, to warn them.

**c4** (11:27, 23:24): The leaders who disbelieved said that they saw him only as a human being like themselves.

**c5** (11:27, 26:111): They said that only the lowliest among them followed him, and asked whether they should believe him when the lowliest followed him.

**c6** (23:24): They said that he wished to gain superiority over them, that God would have sent down angels if He had willed, and that they had not heard of such a thing among their forefathers.

**c7** (23:25): They said that he was only a man with madness, and that they should wait for him for a time.

**c8** (54:9): Another passage says that they called Nuh mad and that he was driven off.

**c9** (11:28): Nuh said that he was on a clear proof from his Lord and had been given mercy from Him, which had been hidden from them, and asked whether he could force it on them while they disliked it.

**c10** (11:29, 26:114): Nuh said that he asked them for no wealth for it, that his reward was only with God, and that he would not drive away the believers, who would meet their Lord.

**c11** (11:30): Nuh asked who would help him against God if he drove the believers away.

**c12** (11:31): Nuh said that he did not claim to hold God's treasures, did not know the unseen, and did not claim to be an angel, and that he would not say that God would never give good to those whom they looked down on.

**c13** (26:112, 26:113, 26:115): Nuh said that he had no knowledge of what they used to do, that their reckoning was only with his Lord, and that he was only a plain warner.

**c14** (26:116): They said that if he did not stop, he would be among those who are stoned.

**c15** (11:32, 11:33, 11:34): They told him that he had argued with them at length and to bring what he threatened if he was truthful; he replied that only God would bring it, if He willed, that they could not escape, and that his advice would not benefit them if God wished to let them go astray.

### One-minute summary

The leaders of Nuh's people rejected him as a human being like themselves who was followed only by the lowly, and called him mad; Nuh answered that he was a messenger and a plain warner who asked no reward and would not drive away the believers [c4][c5][c7][c10][c13].

### Complete story

The leaders of Nuh's people said they saw him in clear error [c1]. Nuh answered that he was not in error but a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, delivering his Lord's messages, advising them, and knowing from God what they did not know [c2]. He asked whether they were astonished that a reminder from their Lord had come on a man from among them to warn them [c3].

The leaders who disbelieved said that they saw him only as a human being like themselves [c4]. They said that only the lowliest among them followed him, and asked whether they should believe him when the lowliest followed him [c5]. They said he wished to gain superiority over them, that God would have sent down angels if He had willed, and that they had not heard of such a thing among their forefathers [c6]. They also said he was a man with madness, and that they should wait for him for a time [c7]; another passage reports that they called him mad and that he was driven off [c8].

Nuh replied that he was on a clear proof from his Lord and had been given mercy from Him, which had been hidden from them; he asked whether he could force it on them while they disliked it [c9]. He said he asked them for no wealth and that his reward was only with God, and that he would not drive away the believers, who would meet their Lord [c10]. He asked who would help him against God if he drove them away [c11]. He did not claim to hold God's treasures, to know the unseen or to be an angel, nor would he say that God would never give good to those whom they looked down on [c12]. He said he had no knowledge of what they used to do, that their reckoning was only with his Lord, and that he was only a plain warner [c13].

They said that if he did not stop, he would be among those who are stoned [c14]. They also told him that he had argued with them at length and to bring what he threatened if he was truthful; he replied that only God would bring it, if He willed, that they could not escape, and that his advice would not benefit them if God wished to let them go astray [c15].

### Deep study

The objections are worded differently in each passage: that he is in error (7:60) [c1], that he is only a human being (11:27, 23:24) [c4], that the lowly follow him (11:27, 26:111) [c5], and that he is mad (23:25, 54:9) [c7][c8]. Nuh's replies are spread in the same way: his messengership (7:61-62) [c2], his proof and mercy (11:28) [c9], and his refusal to drive away the believers (11:29, 26:114) [c10].

### Kids mode

The leaders of Nuh's people said he was only a person like them [c4]. They said that only the lowly followed him [c5]. Nuh said he was a messenger and a warner, that he asked for no reward, and that he would not send the believers away [c2][c10][c13].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The leaders judged the message by who delivered it and who followed it: a human being like themselves, followed by people they looked down on [c4][c5]. One reading is that the passage warns against judging a message by the standing of those who follow it [c5][c10].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not name the leaders of Nuh's people or any individual among them or among the believers.
- It does not say how many followed Nuh or how many opposed him.
- It does not date these exchanges or give their order; the same arguments are reported in different surahs, and this chapter groups them by theme, not by time.
- The verse 11:35 (a question whether they say he invented it) is a separate aside whose speaker is not clear from the verse; it is not used here and a reviewer should decide.

## 3. The long call  (`#the-long-call`)

Cited ayat: 10:71-72, 29:14, 71:5-20

> **10:71** وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ إِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُم مَّقَامِى وَتَذْكِيرِى بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ فَأَجْمِعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً ثُمَّ ٱقْضُوٓا۟ إِلَىَّ وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ
>
> **10:72** فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَمَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

> **29:14** وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ

> **71:5** قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِى لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
>
> **71:6** فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعَآءِىٓ إِلَّا فِرَارًا
>
> **71:7** وَإِنِّى كُلَّمَا دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوٓا۟ أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَٱسْتَغْشَوْا۟ ثِيَابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا۟ وَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ ٱسْتِكْبَارًا
>
> **71:8** ثُمَّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهَارًا
>
> **71:9** ثُمَّ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَنتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًا
>
> **71:10** فَقُلْتُ ٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارًا
>
> **71:11** يُرْسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًا
>
> **71:12** وَيُمْدِدْكُم بِأَمْوَٰلٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ جَنَّٰتٍ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ أَنْهَٰرًا
>
> **71:13** مَّا لَكُمْ لَا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارًا
>
> **71:14** وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا
>

>
> **71:16** وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا
>
> **71:17** وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا
>
> **71:18** ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا
>
> **71:19** وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا
>
> **71:20** لِّتَسْلُكُوا۟ مِنْهَا سُبُلًا فِجَاجًا

### Claims

**c1** (29:14): Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years.

**c2** (71:5, 71:6): Nuh told God that he had called his people night and day, and that his calling only increased their flight.

**c3** (71:7): Nuh said that each time he called them so that God might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were extremely arrogant.

**c4** (71:8, 71:9): Nuh said that he called them openly, and also spoke to them publicly and in private.

**c5** (71:10, 71:11, 71:12): Nuh told them to ask their Lord for forgiveness, for He is ever forgiving, and said that He would then send rain upon them in abundance, increase them with wealth and sons, and give them gardens and rivers.

**c6** (71:13, 71:14): Nuh asked what was the matter with them that they did not look for dignity from God, when He had created them in stages.

**c7** (71:15, 71:16): Nuh pointed to the heavens, seven one above another, and to the moon as a light and the sun as a lamp.

**c8** (71:17, 71:18, 71:19, 71:20): Nuh reminded them that God caused them to grow from the earth, will return them into it and bring them out again, and has spread the earth for them so that they may walk its wide paths.

**c9** (10:71): In another passage Nuh told his people that if his standing among them and his reminders of God's signs weighed on them, he relied on God, and they could gather their plan with their partners and act against him without giving him respite.

**c10** (10:72): Nuh told them that if they turned away, he had asked them for no reward, that his reward was only with God, and that he was commanded to be among those who submit.

### One-minute summary

Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years, called them night and day, openly and in private, and reminded them of God's signs, but they turned away [c1][c2][c4][c7][c3].

### Complete story

The Quran says Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years [c1]. He told God he had called his people night and day, and that his calling only increased their flight [c2]. Each time he called them so that God might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were extremely arrogant [c3]. He called them openly, and he also spoke to them publicly and in private [c4].

He told them to ask their Lord for forgiveness, for He is ever forgiving, and said that He would then send rain upon them in abundance, increase them with wealth and sons, and give them gardens and rivers [c5]. He asked what was the matter with them that they did not look for dignity from God, when He had created them in stages [c6]. He pointed to the heavens, seven one above another, and to the moon as a light and the sun as a lamp [c7]. He reminded them that God caused them to grow from the earth, will return them into it and bring them out again, and has spread the earth for them so that they may walk its wide paths [c8].

In another passage Nuh tells his people that if his standing among them and his reminders of God's signs weigh on them, he relies on God, and they may gather their plan with their partners and act against him without giving him respite [c9]. If they turn away, he has asked them for no reward; his reward is only with God, and he was commanded to be among those who submit [c10].

### Deep study

The people's refusal is described by fleeing (71:6) [c2] and by blocking their ears and covering themselves (71:7) [c3]. Nuh's reminders move from his words about forgiveness and its fruits (71:10-12) [c5] to signs in the heavens and on the earth (71:15-20) [c7][c8].

### Kids mode

Nuh called his people for a very long time, night and day, in public and in private [c1][c2][c4]. He reminded them of the sky, the sun, the moon and the earth as signs of God [c7][c8]. But they put their fingers in their ears and would not listen [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage shows calling done in more than one manner: by night and by day, openly and privately, with encouragement and with reminders of God's signs [c2][c4][c5][c7]. One reading is that persistence in a sincere call does not depend on how it is received [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran says Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years. It does not say whether this is his whole life or only the time he spent calling them.
- It does not say when the calling began or ended, or how the time divides among the ways of calling described here.
- The Arabic word in 71:13 (rendered 'dignity') is read in more than one way, for example as dignity given by God or as God's own majesty; this draft does not decide.
- The promises of rain, wealth, sons, gardens and rivers are reported as Nuh's words to his people; the verses do not say that anyone received them.
- The order of 10:71-72 relative to the rest is not stated.

## 4. Nuh's complaint and prayer  (`#complaint-and-prayer`)

Cited ayat: 11:36, 23:26, 26:117-118, 54:10, 71:21-28

> **11:36** وَأُوحِىَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدْ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ

> **23:26** قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ

> **26:117** قَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِى كَذَّبُونِ
>
> **26:118** فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

> **54:10** فَدَعَا رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَغْلُوبٌ فَٱنتَصِرْ

> **71:21** قَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِى وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
>
> **71:22** وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًا كُبَّارًا
>
> **71:23** وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
>
> **71:24** وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًا وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلًا
>
> **71:25** مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًا
>
> **71:26** وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
>
> **71:27** إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا۟ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا
>
> **71:28** رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا

### Claims

**c1** (11:36): It was revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, so he should not be distressed by what they did.

**c2** (71:21, 71:22): Nuh told God that his people had disobeyed him and followed one whose wealth and children only increased his loss, and that they had plotted a great plot.

**c3** (71:23, 71:24): They told one another not to abandon their gods, and not to abandon Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq and Nasr; Nuh said they had led many astray, and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in error.

**c4** (71:25): Because of their wrongs they were drowned and then made to enter a fire, and they found no helpers besides God.

**c5** (71:26, 71:27): Nuh asked God not to leave on the earth anyone of the disbelievers dwelling there, because if God left them they would mislead His servants and beget only wicked, ungrateful children.

**c6** (71:28): Nuh asked forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever entered his house as a believer, and the believing men and women, and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in ruin.

**c7** (26:117, 26:118): Nuh said that his people had denied him, and asked God to open a decisive judgement between him and them and to save him and the believers with him.

**c8** (54:10, 23:26): Nuh called on his Lord that he was overcome and asked for help, because they had denied him.

### One-minute summary

God told Nuh that no more of his people would believe; Nuh complained to God of their refusal and their plotting, prayed for the believers, and asked for help [c1][c2][c6][c8].

### Complete story

God revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, and that he should not be distressed by what they did [c1]. Nuh told God that his people had disobeyed him and followed one whose wealth and children only increased his loss, and that they had plotted a great plot [c2]. They told one another not to abandon their gods, and named Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq and Nasr [c3]. Nuh said they had led many astray and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in error [c3].

The Quran adds that because of their wrongs they were drowned and then made to enter a fire, and that they found no helpers besides God [c4].

Nuh asked God not to leave anyone of the disbelievers dwelling on the earth, since, he said, if God left them they would mislead His servants and beget only wicked, ungrateful children [c5]. He asked forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever entered his house as a believer, and the believing men and women, and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in ruin [c6]. In other passages he says that his people had denied him and asks God to judge decisively between them and him and to save him and the believers with him [c7]; he calls on his Lord that he is overcome and asks for help [c8].

### Deep study

Nuh's requests are worded in different ways: that God judge between them and him [c7], that God help him because he is overcome [c8], and that God not leave anyone of the disbelievers dwelling on the earth [c5]. The names of the gods are given only in the passage at 71:23 [c3].

### Kids mode

God told Nuh that no more of his people would believe, so he should not be sad about what they did [c1]. Nuh asked God for help and to save him and the believers [c7][c8]. He asked God to forgive him, his parents and the believers [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage shows Nuh bringing his distress to God in words [c7][c8]. One reading is that taking hardship to God in prayer is presented here as the answer to rejection [c8]. In his prayer he also asks forgiveness for himself and for the believers, and not only relief [c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not say when, within the long period of calling, these prayers were made, or whether they came before or after the order to build the ship. This chapter groups them by theme.
- It does not say who or what these names were; the verse gives only the names as the gods the people held to. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts say who they were; none is used here.
- It does not say whom the phrase 'one whose wealth and children only increased his loss' points to; it may mean a person or a kind of person.
- It does not name Nuh's parents.
- The verse 71:25 says they were drowned and then made to enter a fire; it does not say when this fire is entered or describe it.

## 5. Building the ship  (`#building-the-ship`)

Cited ayat: 11:36-39, 23:27

> **11:36** وَأُوحِىَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدْ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ
>
> **11:37** وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ
>
> **11:38** وَيَصْنَعُ ٱلْفُلْكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌ مِّن قَوْمِهِۦ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُ قَالَ إِن تَسْخَرُوا۟ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسْخَرُ مِنكُمْ كَمَا تَسْخَرُونَ
>
> **11:39** فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن يَأْتِيهِ عَذَابٌ يُخْزِيهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذَابٌ مُّقِيمٌ

> **23:27** فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (11:36, 11:37, 23:27): God revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who already had, and told him to build the ship under His watch and by His revelation.

**c2** (11:37, 23:27): God told Nuh not to speak to Him about those who had done wrong, for they would be drowned.

**c3** (11:38): While Nuh was building the ship, each time leaders of his people passed by him they mocked him.

**c4** (11:38, 11:39): Nuh said that if they mocked him, he would mock them in the same way, and that they would come to know who would receive a punishment that disgraces and a punishment that lasts.

### One-minute summary

At God's command Nuh built the ship, and the leaders of his people mocked him as he built it [c1][c3].

### Complete story

God revealed to Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who already had, and told him to build the ship under His watch and by His revelation [c1]. He told him not to speak to Him about those who had done wrong, for they would be drowned [c2]. As Nuh built it, whenever leaders of his people passed by they mocked him [c3]. He said that if they mocked him, he would mock them in the same way, and that they would come to know who would receive a punishment that disgraces and a punishment that lasts [c4].

### Deep study

The command to build the ship is worded almost alike at 11:37 and 23:27 [c1][c2]. It comes with a prohibition: Nuh is not to plead for the wrongdoers [c2].

### Kids mode

God told Nuh to build a ship [c1]. The leaders of his people laughed at him as he built it [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Nuh keeps building while he is mocked [c3][c4]. One reading is that a task given by God is carried on in spite of ridicule [c1][c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not give the ship's size, its shape, the materials beyond those named in the next chapter, the place where it was built, or how long it took.
- It does not say what the people did, apart from mocking, while the ship was being built.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts give dimensions, a building place and a timeline for the ship; none is used here.

> **11:41** وَقَالَ ٱرْكَبُوا۟ فِيهَا بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ مَجْر۪ىٰهَا وَمُرْسَىٰهَآ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
>
> **11:42** وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

> **23:27** فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ
>
> **23:28** فَإِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتَ أَنتَ وَمَن مَّعَكَ عَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ فَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى نَجَّىٰنَا مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
>
> **23:29** وَقُل رَّبِّ أَنزِلْنِى مُنزَلًا مُّبَارَكًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ

> **26:119** فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
>
> **26:120** ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا بَعْدُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ

> **54:11** فَفَتَحْنَآ أَبْوَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَآءٍ مُّنْهَمِرٍ
>
> **54:12** وَفَجَّرْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا فَٱلْتَقَى ٱلْمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ
>
> **54:13** وَحَمَلْنَٰهُ عَلَىٰ ذَاتِ أَلْوَٰحٍ وَدُسُرٍ
>
> **54:14** تَجْرِى بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ

### Claims

**c1** (11:40, 23:27): When God's command came and the tannur (a word usually rendered oven) boiled over, God told Nuh to carry on the ship a pair of every kind, and his family, except those against whom the word had already gone out, and those who believed; few had believed with him.

**c2** (11:41): Nuh told them to embark and said that in God's name was its sailing and its anchoring, for his Lord is forgiving and merciful.

**c3** (23:28, 23:29): God told Nuh to say, once he and those with him were settled on the ship, that praise belongs to God who had saved them from the wrongdoing people, and to ask to be landed at a blessed landing place.

**c4** (54:11, 54:12): God opened the gates of heaven with pouring water and made the earth burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed.

**c5** (54:13, 54:14): God carried Nuh on a vessel of planks and dusur (a word often rendered nails or fibres), which sailed under His watch, as a reward for one who had been rejected.

**c6** (11:42): The ship sailed with them through waves like mountains.

**c7** (7:64, 26:119, 26:120): God saved Nuh and those with him in the laden ship and drowned the rest, who had denied His signs.

### One-minute summary

When God's command came, Nuh carried on the ship a pair of every kind, his family (except those against whom the word had gone out) and the believers; water poured from the sky and burst from the earth, and the ship sailed through waves like mountains [c1][c4][c6]. God saved Nuh and those with him and drowned the rest [c7].

### Complete story

When God's command came and the tannur (a word usually rendered oven) boiled over, God told Nuh to carry on the ship a pair of every kind, and his family, except those against whom the word had already gone out, and those who believed; few had believed with him [c1]. Nuh told them to embark and said that in God's name was its sailing and its anchoring, for his Lord is forgiving and merciful [c2]. God told Nuh to say, once he and those with him were settled on the ship, that praise belongs to God who had saved them from the wrongdoing people, and to ask to be landed at a blessed landing place [c3].

The Quran describes the flood in these terms: God opened the gates of heaven with pouring water and made the earth burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed [c4]. He carried Nuh on a vessel of planks and dusur (a word often rendered nails or fibres), which sailed under His watch, as a reward for one who had been rejected [c5]. It sailed with them through waves like mountains [c6]. God saved Nuh and those with him in the laden ship and drowned the rest [c7].

### Deep study

The flood is told from different sides: the sign and the command to embark [c1], Nuh's words on boarding [c2][c3], the description of the waters [c4], the vessel [c5] and the waves [c6]. The outcome is the same in every passage that tells it: Nuh and those with him are saved and the rest are drowned [c7].

### Kids mode

When God's command came, water poured from the sky and sprang up from the earth [c4]. Nuh took on the ship a pair of every kind, his family (except those about whom God's word had gone out), and the believers [c1]. The ship sailed through waves like mountains [c6]. God saved Nuh and those with him [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Nuh's words on boarding give thanks to God for rescue and ask for a blessed landing [c2][c3]. One reading is that gratitude and prayer are joined at the moment of safety [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not say what the tannur was or where it was; 'oven' is a common rendering and its sense is discussed.
- It does not say how many people were on the ship, which animals were carried or how many kinds, or how they were gathered and cared for.
- It does not say how long the flood lasted, how deep the water rose, or whether the water covered the whole earth or only the region of Nuh's people. A scholar should decide how to word the extent for readers.
- The Arabic word dusur is explained as nails and as fibres; this draft does not decide.
- Which members of Nuh's family were taken and which were not is not stated beyond 'those against whom the word had gone out'; the next chapter tells of his son.
- The Quran does not name the passengers.

## 7. Nuh and his son  (`#nuh-and-his-son`)

Cited ayat: 11:42-43, 11:45-47

> **11:42** وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
>
> **11:43** قَالَ سَـَٔاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِى مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُغْرَقِينَ

> **11:45** وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبْنِى مِنْ أَهْلِى وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ
>
> **11:46** قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَٰلِحٍ فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ إِنِّىٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
>
> **11:47** قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِى وَتَرْحَمْنِىٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (11:42): Nuh called out to his son, who was standing apart, to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers.

**c2** (11:43): The son said he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water; Nuh replied that nothing that day protects from God's command except for the one on whom He has mercy; the wave came between them, and the son was among the drowned.

**c3** (11:45): Nuh called to his Lord, saying that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that He is the most just of judges.

**c4** (11:46): God answered that the son was not of Nuh's family, that his deed was not righteous, and that Nuh should not ask Him about what he had no knowledge of; God advised him not to be among the ignorant.

**c5** (11:47): Nuh said that he sought refuge in God from asking what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him he would be among the losers.

### One-minute summary

Nuh called to his son to board; the son refused, the wave came between them and he was drowned [c1][c2]. Nuh appealed to God about him, God answered that he was not of Nuh's family because his deed was not righteous, and Nuh asked forgiveness [c3][c4][c5].

### Complete story

As the ship sailed through the waves, Nuh called out to his son, who was standing apart, to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers [c1]. The son said he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water [c2]. Nuh replied that nothing that day protects from God's command except for the one on whom He has mercy; then the wave came between them, and the son was among the drowned [c2].

Nuh called to his Lord, saying that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that He is the most just of judges [c3]. God answered that the son was not of Nuh's family, that his deed was not righteous, and that Nuh should not ask Him about what he had no knowledge of; God advised him not to be among the ignorant [c4]. Nuh said that he sought refuge in God from asking what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him he would be among the losers [c5].

### Deep study

God's answer in 11:46 gives a reason for the statement that the son is not of Nuh's family: his deed was not righteous [c4]. The passage ends with Nuh asking forgiveness for the question itself [c5].

### Kids mode

Nuh called to his son to come on the ship, but the son would not come and was among those drowned [c1][c2]. Nuh asked God about his son, and God told him not to ask about what he did not know [c3][c4]. Nuh asked God to forgive him [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage shows a father asking on behalf of his son, and the answer given to him [c3][c4]. One reading is that family ties are not treated here as a ground of rescue by themselves, since the verse gives the son's deed as the reason [c4]. Another is that a prophet, on being corrected, turns to seeking God's forgiveness [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not name Nuh's son, or say why he stood apart or what he believed. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts give the son a name; it is not used here.
- It does not say how old the son was or whether he had a family.
- The wording of 11:46 ('his deed was not righteous') can be read in more than one way in the Arabic; this draft keeps the plainest rendering and a reviewer should check it.
- It does not say whether other relatives were among those not carried.

## 8. The waters recede  (`#the-waters-recede`)

Cited ayat: 11:44, 11:48

> **11:44** وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِى مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقْلِعِى وَغِيضَ ٱلْمَآءُ وَقُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِىِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

> **11:48** قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (11:44): A command was given that the earth swallow its water and the sky hold back; the water subsided and the matter was decreed.

**c2** (11:44): The ship settled on Judi (with the Arabic article, al-Judi), and it was announced that the wrongdoing people were to be far removed.

**c3** (11:48): Nuh was told to come down in peace from God and with blessings upon him and upon communities from those with him; and there would be other communities whom God would let enjoy life for a time, and then a painful punishment from Him would touch them.

### One-minute summary

At God's command the water subsided and the ship settled on Judi; Nuh was told to come down in peace and with blessings [c1][c2][c3].

### Complete story

A command was given that the earth swallow its water and the sky hold back; the water subsided, the matter was decreed, and the ship settled on Judi (with the Arabic article, al-Judi) [c1][c2]. It was announced that the wrongdoing people were to be far removed [c2].

Nuh was told to come down in peace from God and with blessings upon him and upon communities from those with him [c3]. There would be other communities, God said, whom He would let enjoy life for a time, and then a painful punishment from Him would touch them [c3].

### Deep study

The ending in 11:44 is told in short successive clauses, from the command to the earth and the sky to the settling of the ship and the closing word on the wrongdoers [c1][c2]. In 11:48 the blessing is on Nuh and on communities from those with him, and a warning follows for later communities [c3].

### Kids mode

The water went down, and the ship rested on Judi [c1][c2]. God told Nuh to come down in peace, with blessings on him and on those with him [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): In the text the account ends with peace and blessing for Nuh and those with him, and with a warning to later communities [c3]. One reading is that the passage looks past the flood to what follows it [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran names Judi as where the ship settled; it does not say where Judi is. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts identify Judi with particular mountains, one of them Ararat; none is used here.
- It does not say how long the water took to subside or how long they stayed on the ship.
- It does not say who the 'communities' of 11:48 are, or how they relate to the peoples who came later.

## 9. A sign that remains  (`#a-sign-that-remains`)

Cited ayat: 10:73, 23:30, 26:121-122, 29:15, 37:75-82, 54:15-17

> **10:73** فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ خَلَٰٓئِفَ وَأَغْرَقْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

> **23:30** إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ وَإِن كُنَّا لَمُبْتَلِينَ

> **26:121** إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **26:122** وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

> **29:15** فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَصْحَٰبَ ٱلسَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ

> **37:75** وَلَقَدْ نَادَىٰنَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ
>
> **37:76** وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
>
> **37:77** وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥ هُمُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
>
> **37:78** وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ
>
> **37:79** سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
>
> **37:80** إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
>
> **37:81** إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **37:82** ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْـَٔاخَرِينَ

> **54:15** وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَٰهَآ ءَايَةً فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
>
> **54:16** فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ
>
> **54:17** وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ

### Claims

**c1** (29:15, 54:15): God saved Nuh and the people of the ship and made it a sign for the worlds; He says that He left it as a sign.

**c2** (54:15, 54:16, 54:17): God asks whether there is anyone who will take heed, asks how His punishment and warnings were, and says that He has made the Quran easy for remembrance.

**c3** (10:73): God saved Nuh and those with him in the ship, made them successors, drowned those who denied His signs, and told the hearer to look at the end of those who had been warned.

**c4** (37:75, 37:76): Nuh called to God, and God says how excellent are those who answer; He saved Nuh and his family from the great distress.

**c5** (37:77): God made Nuh's offspring the survivors.

**c6** (37:78, 37:79, 37:80, 37:81): God left on Nuh among later generations a declaration of peace upon Nuh among the worlds; this is how He rewards those who do good, and Nuh was among His believing servants.

**c7** (37:82): Then God drowned the others.

**c8** (26:121, 26:122, 23:30): The Quran says that there is a sign in this, though most of them were not believers, that God is the Mighty, the Merciful, that there are signs in it, and that God is always testing.

### One-minute summary

God saved Nuh and those with him, made the ship a sign, made his offspring the survivors, and left a declaration of peace upon him among later generations [c1][c3][c5][c6].

### Complete story

God saved Nuh and the people of the ship and made it a sign for the worlds [c1]. He asks whether there is anyone who will take heed, asks how His punishment and warnings were, and says the Quran has been made easy for remembrance [c2]. The Quran says that God made those with Nuh successors, drowned those who denied His signs, and tells the hearer to look at the end of those who had been warned [c3].

Nuh called to God, and God says how excellent are those who answer; He saved Nuh and his family from the great distress [c4]. He made Nuh's offspring the survivors [c5], and drowned the others [c7]. God left on Nuh, among later generations, a declaration of peace upon Nuh among the worlds, and the Quran says that this is how God rewards those who do good, and that Nuh was among His believing servants [c6].

The Quran says there is a sign in this, though most of them were not believers, and that God is the Mighty, the Merciful; it adds that there are signs in it, and that God is always testing [c8].

### Deep study

The outcome is told in more than one way: as rescue and a sign (29:15, 54:15) [c1], as succession (10:73) [c3], as the survival of Nuh's offspring (37:77) [c5], and as lasting remembrance (37:78-79) [c6]. Some passages end by calling the account a sign [c8][c1].

### Kids mode

God saved Nuh and those with him and made the ship a sign [c1]. God sent peace upon Nuh, and the Quran says he was one of God's believing servants [c6]. The Quran asks whether anyone will take heed [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The account is called a sign and a reminder, and the Quran asks whether anyone will take heed [c1][c2]. One reading is that the story is offered as a reminder to take heed [c2]. The text also says that God is always testing [c8].

### What the sources do not establish

- The Quran does not say how long Nuh lived after the flood, where he settled, or when or where he died.
- It says that Nuh's offspring were the survivors; it does not list them. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later accounts name sons and give each a line of descent; none is used here.
- It does not say what became of the ship after it came to rest.
- The short passages 37:75-82 and 54:15-17 summarise the outcome; they add no events.
